issues.t: Pre-catalyst breaks apart and scores the cylinders
issues.sym: The engine starts using oil between changes, the oil looks dirty, a rattle comes from the exhaust manifold area, or new knocking and low power appear.
issues.why: The small catalytic converter built into the exhaust manifold on the early 2.5L can overheat and crumble. Pieces get pulled back into the cylinders and wear the walls, which leads to oil burning and lost compression. On 2002 cars Nissan also found an exhaust hanger pin that could catch road debris, and recalled them for fire risk.
issues.next: Run the VIN for recall 03V-084 (2002 models). On any year, if oil use climbs or the engine starts knocking, stop driving it hard and have the pre-cat and compression checked before the engine is damaged.

issues.t: Engine stalls at low speed from crank sensor signal dropouts (recall)
issues.sym: The engine shuts off without warning while slowing down or driving at low speed, sometimes with no warning light.
issues.why: Heat can make the crankshaft position sensor briefly lose its signal. The dropout is too short for the engine computer to flag, so the engine simply stops. Nissan recalled 2003-2004 cars first and later added 2002 and 2005-2006 cars, reprogramming the engine computer.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check the VIN for recalls 06V-242 and 07V-527 and have the reprogramming done. If the car stalls, get it diagnosed before relying on it in traffic.

issues.t: Long cranking before the engine starts
issues.sym: The starter turns the engine over for several seconds before it catches, most often after the car has sat.
issues.why: Nissan issued a service bulletin for 2002-2006 Sentras that crank longer than normal before starting, with a dealer repair procedure.
issues.next: Mention bulletin NTB05-052 to the shop. Also have the battery and fuel pressure checked so a different fault is not missed.

issues.t: Takata passenger airbag inflator can rupture (do-not-drive recall)
issues.sym: Usually nothing before a crash. The danger is hidden.
issues.why: The passenger front airbag inflator can burst in a crash and throw metal fragments. Some temporary replacement inflators were also defective, and some cars were missed during earlier inspections, so Nissan told owners of those cars not to drive them.
issues.next: Check the VIN right away for recalls 15V-287, 20V-008 and 20V-747. If any are open, do not drive the car or let anyone ride in front until the inflator is replaced.

issues.t: Brake master cylinder leaks internally (recall)
issues.sym: The brake warning light comes on, the pedal travels farther than normal, or stopping takes longer.
issues.why: The brake master cylinder could leak inside itself, which can take one of the two brake circuits out of action. Nissan recalled affected cars and later added more 2008 models.
issues.next: If the brake pedal sinks, feels soft or goes closer to the floor, or a red brake warning comes on, slow down gently, use a lower gear, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on: call for a tow. If the brake warning light comes on, have the brakes checked before driving further. Run the VIN for recalls 08V-311 and 09V-431.

issues.t: CVT whine, shudder or slipping
issues.sym: A whining or droning noise that rises with speed, shudder or hesitation when pulling away, or the engine revving without the car gaining speed.
issues.why: The first-generation CVT used in this Sentra wears internally, especially when it runs hot or the fluid is old. Nissan extended CVT coverage on 2007-2010 cars, and transmission problems are the most complained-about area on the Sentra.
issues.next: Have the CVT fluid and the transmission checked at the first sign of whine or slipping, and change the fluid on schedule. Nissan once extended CVT coverage on these cars to ten years, but that period has run out on nearly all of them, so repairs are now on the owner. If the car loses drive, have it towed rather than driven.

issues.t: Battery terminal stud causes hard starts and stalling (recall)
issues.sym: Hard starting, flickering lights, or the engine stalling, often at low speed.
issues.why: The zinc coating on the battery terminal stud was too thick, so the cable did not make a solid connection and voltage could drop.
issues.next: Run the VIN for recall 11V-579 and have the terminal repaired.

issues.t: CVT shudder, hesitation and failure
issues.sym: Shudder or judder when pulling away or climbing hills, hesitation, a whining noise, a transmission warning light, or the car going into a low-power limp mode.
issues.why: The CVT in this generation is prone to internal wear and overheating. Class-action settlements extended CVT coverage on 2013-2017 cars and on 2018-2019 cars, and the 2014-2015 models draw the most transmission failure complaints.
issues.next: Get it checked at the first shudder or whine, and ask a dealer whether any extended coverage still applies. If the car enters limp mode or loses drive, stop driving it and have it towed.

issues.t: Passenger airbag turned off with an adult seated (recalls)
issues.sym: The PASSENGER AIRBAG OFF light is lit even though an adult is sitting in the front seat.
issues.why: The occupant classification system under the passenger seat can misread the seat as empty or holding a child, and then switches the airbag off. Nissan issued software and sensor recalls.
issues.next: Run the VIN for recalls 14V-138 and 16V-244. Until fixed, seat adult passengers in the back when the OFF light is on with someone in front.

issues.t: Passenger seat belt bracket can bend with a child seat (recall)
issues.sym: After installing a child seat in front, the passenger airbag may stay on instead of turning off.
issues.why: Tightening a child seat with the belt can bend the passenger belt bracket, which confuses the occupant sensor so the airbag is not suppressed.
issues.next: Run the VIN for recall 16V-242. Children belong in the back seat regardless.

issues.t: Passenger airbag inflator may not deploy correctly (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no symptom before a crash.
issues.why: A manufacturing error in some passenger airbag inflators could keep the airbag from inflating properly. Some 2014 cars are included too.
issues.next: Run the VIN for recall 17V-253 and have the inflator replaced.

issues.t: Brake lights may not come on (recall)
issues.sym: Brake lights stay dark when you press the pedal. Drivers behind may honk or follow too closely, and you usually cannot tell from inside the car.
issues.why: Contamination inside the brake light switch can stop it from working, so drivers behind get no warning that you are slowing.
issues.next: Have someone check your brake lights and run the VIN for recall 21V-135. Get the switch replaced promptly.

issues.t: Ignition key can slip out of Run (recall)
issues.sym: The engine shuts off and power steering and brake assist are lost after a bump, often with a heavy key ring.
issues.why: The ignition could move from Run to Accessory when jarred, cutting the engine.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Take extra weight off the key ring and run the VIN for recall 18V-551.

issues.t: Front tie rods can bend or break (recall)
issues.sym: The steering wheel sits off-center, the car pulls, tires wear unevenly, or steering suddenly stops responding normally, often after hitting a curb or pothole.
issues.why: The front tie rods on this generation can bend under a hard impact and later break, which can cause loss of steering control. Nissan recalled the cars and then widened the recall.
issues.next: Run the VIN for recalls 21V-461 and 23V-581. If the wheel is off-center after an impact, have the tie rods inspected before driving normally.

issues.t: Rearview camera image distorted or blank (recall)
issues.sym: The backup camera shows a distorted, flickering or blank picture.
issues.why: The camera wiring can be damaged so the image does not reach the screen reliably.
issues.next: Run the VIN for recall 23V-628. Back up with extra care until it is fixed.

issues.t: Driver airbag inflator may deploy improperly (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no symptom before a crash.
issues.why: Moisture can get into the driver airbag inflator, which may make it deploy abnormally in a crash.
issues.next: Run the VIN for recall 24V-154 and have the airbag module replaced.

issues.t: Left front driveshaft not fully seated in the CVT (recall)
issues.sym: Transmission fluid dripping near the front left wheel, a clunk, or a sudden loss of drive power. The car may roll if parked without the parking brake.
issues.why: On some cars the left driveshaft was not fully pushed into the transmission or its retaining clip was loose or missing, so it can work loose and leak fluid.
issues.next: Run the VIN for recalls 24V-304 (2024) and 26V-410 (2025). If you see fluid under the front or lose drive, stop driving and have it towed. Always set the parking brake.

issues.t: Door striker welds can break (recall)
issues.sym: A door that does not latch firmly or rattles when closed.
issues.why: Poorly welded door strikers can break, which could let a door open while driving.
issues.next: Run the VIN for recall 26V-023 and have the strikers inspected. Make sure every door is fully latched before driving.

issues.t: Air bubbles in the windshield glass (recall)
issues.sym: Bubbles or flaws in the windshield that distort the driver's view.
issues.why: A glass defect left air bubbles in some windshields.
issues.next: Run the VIN for recall 25V-807 and have the windshield replaced if affected.

issues.t: Head gasket fails on the 1.8L engine
issues.sym: Coolant level keeps dropping with no puddle under the car, the temperature gauge climbs, white sweet-smelling smoke comes from the tailpipe, or the engine runs rough on a cold start.
issues.why: The head gasket on the 1.8L engine in this generation is a repeated owner complaint. Once it starts to seep, coolant gets into the cylinders or the oil, and any overheating makes the damage worse quickly.
issues.next: Do not keep driving a car that is overheating or losing coolant. Have a shop pressure-test the cooling system and check for combustion gas in the coolant before the engine is damaged.

issues.t: Wipers can quit when the linkage joint wears out (recall)
issues.sym: One or both wipers slow down, stop part way across the glass or stop moving at all, often in heavy rain.
issues.why: Water washes the grease out of a ball joint in the wiper linkage, so the joint wears and finally comes apart.
issues.next: Have the wiper linkage checked and replaced before you drive in rain or snow; losing the wipers takes your view away in seconds.

issues.t: Tail lights are dimmer than the safety rules allow (recall)
issues.sym: Drivers behind you may not pick up the tail lights in daylight or rain, and you may get flashed or honked at.
issues.why: The tail lamp assemblies were built so they do not put out as much light as the federal lighting standard requires.
issues.next: Ask a Nissan dealer whether the lamp replacement for this campaign was done, and check your lights are clean and working.

issues.t: Front coil spring can corrode and break (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk or bang from a front corner, the car sits lower on one side, or a front tire suddenly loses air.
issues.why: Road salt corrodes the front coil springs; a rusted spring can snap and the broken end can cut into the tire.
issues.next: Stop driving and have the front springs inspected if you hear a bang or the car drops on one corner, because a cut tire can let go at speed.

issues.t: Rear door impact pad may be missing (recall)
issues.sym: Nothing you can feel day to day; it only matters in a side impact.
issues.why: Some cars left the plant without the foam pad that is meant to be fitted inside the rear door to soften a side hit.
issues.next: Have a Nissan dealer check the campaign against your VIN so the missing pad can be installed.

issues.t: Crank position sensor can shut the engine off (recall)
issues.sym: The engine cuts out while driving or will not restart once it is warm, sometimes with the check engine light on.
issues.why: Some crank position sensors were built wrong and stop telling the computer where the engine is, so spark and fuel stop.
issues.next: Get the sensor replaced soon; a stall in traffic or on a highway ramp is dangerous.

issues.t: Solder joint in the sensor circuit board can crack (recall)
issues.sym: Random stalling, a long crank before it fires, or the engine quits and starts again on its own.
issues.why: A solder joint on the crank and cam sensor circuit board can crack, breaking the signal the engine computer needs.
issues.next: Have the sensors replaced under the campaign rather than chasing the stall; repeated stalling is a safety risk.

issues.t: Steel wheel can crack around the cooling holes (recall)
issues.sym: Vibration or a wobble you can feel through the steering, or a visible crack between the holes in a steel wheel.
issues.why: The cooling holes in some steel wheels were made in a way that lets cracks start and spread.
issues.next: Have the wheels inspected right away, because a cracked wheel can come apart at speed.

issues.t: Lower control arm bolts can break (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk from the front of the car, loose or wandering steering, or a front wheel that looks out of place.
issues.why: The bolts holding the lower control arm to the body can fracture, so the arm can come loose.
issues.next: Stop driving and have it inspected if you hear a clunk from the front, because a loose control arm can cause a crash.

issues.t: Engine computer box foam can corrode the circuit (recall)
issues.sym: Check engine light, odd running or an engine that will not start, with no obvious mechanical fault.
issues.why: Foam inside the engine control module box can give off sulfur, which corrodes resistors on the circuit board.
issues.next: Have the module checked under the campaign before paying for other electrical diagnosis.

issues.t: Piston rings can let the engine burn oil (recall)
issues.sym: The oil level drops between changes, there may be blue smoke from the tailpipe and the oil light may flicker.
issues.why: Piston rings in some engines were not made to spec, so oil gets past them into the combustion chambers.
issues.next: Keep the oil topped up and have the engine checked under the campaign; running it low on oil can destroy it.

issues.t: Positive battery cable end can lose contact (recall)
issues.sym: Slow or no cranking, flickering lights, or the engine quits at low speed and will not restart.
issues.why: A gap in the crimped end of the positive battery cable adds resistance, so voltage drops under load.
issues.next: Have the cable replaced under the campaign soon; stalling in traffic is a safety risk.

issues.t: Dealer navigation unit battery can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: The portable navigation unit gets very hot, smells hot or shows damage around its battery.
issues.why: The lithium battery in the accessory navigation unit supplied with some cars can overheat.
issues.next: Stop using the unit and have it exchanged under the campaign, because an overheating battery can start a fire.

issues.t: Rear camera image can be turned off and stay off (recall)
issues.sym: You shift into reverse and the screen shows the radio or a blank picture instead of the view behind the car.
issues.why: The display settings let the camera image be switched off, and the setting stays off the next time you reverse.
issues.next: Have the software updated under the campaign, and until then check behind the car before backing up.

issues.t: Right headlight may be aimed wrong (recall)
issues.sym: The light pattern on the road looks uneven side to side, or oncoming drivers flash their lights at you.
issues.why: The right headlight was aimed outside the allowed range when the car was built.
issues.next: Have the headlight aim corrected under the campaign so you can see and are not blinding others.

issues.t: Missing cowl seal lets water reach electrical parts (recall)
issues.sym: Damp carpet or a musty smell, and electrical faults such as warning lights or parts that stop working.
issues.why: A seal at the base of the windshield may be missing or wrong, so water runs into the area where electrical parts sit.
issues.next: Have the seal inspected under the campaign before the water corrodes connectors and causes bigger faults.

issues.t: Windshield bubbles can hide the VIN (recall)
issues.sym: Small bubbles in the glass near the bottom of the windshield, sometimes over the VIN plate.
issues.why: Air bubbles were left in the glass when the windshield was made.
issues.next: Have the windshield replaced under the campaign; it is mainly a legal and visibility nuisance, not a breakdown risk.

issues.t: Driver seat may not be fastened to its track (recall)
issues.sym: The driver seat rocks, shifts or feels loose when you get in or brake hard.
issues.why: The seat frame may not have been properly secured to the seat track on the assembly line.
issues.next: Stop driving it and have the seat checked under the campaign, because a loose seat will not hold you in a crash.

issues.t: Front seat frame weld can be weak (recall)
issues.sym: The front seat feels loose or moves more than it should in its mount.
issues.why: A weld on the front seat frame bracket may be weak, so the seat can loosen.
issues.next: Have the seat inspected under the campaign right away; a seat that comes loose in a crash is a serious injury risk.
